clue.text: He-man's opportunity to burn his boats?

definitions.text: He-man's opportunity to burn his boats?

parts.words: He-man's opportunity to burn his boats?
parts.note: 'He-man's' splits into Hemans, Felicia Hemans, whose poem about the boy on the burning deck is the place for burning boats

explanation.surface: A macho man gets his chance to commit himself irrevocably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He-man's' is Felicia Hemans's name pulled apart; her poem 'The boy stood on the burning deck' tells of the boy aboard a burning ship at the Battle of the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Hemans's famous poem is the surname of the boy who stayed on his blazing ship.

clue.text: A circle holding vote for defender of Orestes

indicators.note: the letter A and the ring are said to hold the next piece between them

parts.note: a circle is the round letter O
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A ring of people with a ballot in the middle stands up for a Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: In Aeschylus's Eumenides the god speaks for Orestes at his trial for killing his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Oresteia the god of Delphi acts as advocate for Orestes before the Athenian court.

clue.text: State of Walcott's testament

definitions.meaning: Derek Walcott's 1987 collection of poems is 'The ____ Testament'

explanation.definitionFit: It is a southern US state, and Walcott named a book of poems after it.

clue.text: Possibly game is destruction

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Possibly game is destruction' (10), gives no fodder or wordplay that can make ICONOCLASM; the OCR has evidently lost or garbled part of the clue, and no scan or reprint is available

clue.text: "Profound in all the —— and Real ways beyond them all" (Hudibras, Samuel Butler)

definitions.text: "Profound in all the —— and Real ways beyond them all" (Hudibras, Samuel Butler)

parts.words: "Profound in all the —— and Real ways beyond them all" (Hudibras, Samuel Butler)
parts.note: fill the gap in Butler's satire on the scholastic Hudibras, whose learning covers the rival schools of medieval philosophy

explanation.surface: A line of Butler's mock-heroic Hudibras with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nominal and Real ways are the Nominalist and Realist schools of scholastic philosophy, which Butler's hero has mastered and gone past.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominalism and Realism were the two medieval schools, so the missing word pairs with Real as a philosophical way.

clue.text: Group rhyming scheme?

definitions.meaning: the envelope pattern of a quatrain, first and fourth lines rhyming, second and third rhyming

explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish band's name, and the letters used to chart an enclosed rhyme pattern.

clue.text: Model for Ovid showing some Hellenophile taste

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ovid's exemplar reveals a certain fondness for Greek things.
explanation.walkthrough: Philetas of Cos, the Hellenistic elegiac poet, was named by Ovid and Propertius as a master of love elegy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek elegist of Cos was held up by the Roman love poets as the pattern they followed.

clue.text: Extraordinary knowledge of new prison saga

indicators.note: new says the letters of the two words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel about jail life tells of uncanny knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PRISON SAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means knowing things by supernatural or psychic means.

clue.text: Deity as form of poet-mystery writer

indicators.note: as a form of says the writer's name is rearranged to give a new shape

parts.note: Ernest Bramah, author of the Max Carrados mysteries and the Kai Lung tales

explanation.surface: A god appears as a version of a writer of verse and detective stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as form of' rearranges BRAMAH, the surname of Ernest Bramah; Emerson also wrote a poem with the god's name as its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator god is one of the Hindu trinity with Vishnu and Shiva.

clue.text: Some grub served in the library

definitions.text: Some grub served in the library

parts.words: Some grub served in the library
parts.note: sounds like food on a library menu, but the grub is a larva that feeds on books, and also a keen reader

explanation.surface: A snack is on offer in the reading room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' and 'served' suggest catering; the grub is an insect larva that bores through books, and by extension an avid reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle larva that eats bindings and paper, and a person always reading.

clue.text: Mrs Trundle is a beautiful Italian girl

parts.note: taken as written
bella is Italian for beautiful, used of a girl

explanation.surface: A Pickwickian wife is said to be a lovely Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Pickwick Papers, Mr Wardle's daughter marries Mr Trundle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardle's daughter becomes Mrs Trundle at the Dingley Dell wedding in Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Thom Gunn's manager (handy with a dart?)

definitions.text: Thom Gunn's manager (handy with a dart?)

parts.words: Thom Gunn's manager (handy with a dart?)
parts.note: Gunn's last collection is titled after Cupid as a manager, the god handy with his darts of love

explanation.surface: A poet's employer turns out to be good at darts.
explanation.walkthrough: Thom Gunn's 2000 collection is 'Boss Cupid'; Cupid shoots love's darts, so the clue's manager is handy with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunn's title makes Cupid the one in charge, a word for a manager or employer.

clue.text: Contemporary of Haydn to be rich icon, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters given are one possible arrangement of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A rival of Haydn's might become a wealthy celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BE RICH ICON; Luigi Boccherini (1743-1805) was an Italian composer of Haydn's era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian cellist-composer lived and worked in the same decades as Haydn.

clue.text: Poet gives gossip some weight

parts.note: to chatter is to gossip, as a noun idle talk
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A versifier spreads rumours and puts on a lot of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Chatterton (1752-70) was the boy poet of the Rowley forgeries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bristol youth who forged medieval verse and died at seventeen is a celebrated English versifier.

clue.text: Describing roles for Joan Collins and John Forsythe in Edwardian epic

definitions.text: Describing roles for Joan Collins and John Forsythe
definitions.meaning: the two starred as Alexis and Blake Carrington in the soap opera Dynasty, so they played members of a dynasty
Thomas Hardy's verse drama of the Napoleonic wars, published 1904-08

explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's Napoleonic epic drama shares its name with what the stars of the TV soap Dynasty played.

clue.text: Poet gives credit to a dramatist

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
George Bernard Shaw, the playwright

explanation.surface: A versifier pays tribute to a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Crashaw (c.1613-49) was a metaphysical religious poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century metaphysical writer of religious verse is an English versifier.

clue.text: Old furnaceman retired and somehow gone

parts.note: to be abed is to have retired for the night

indicators.note: somehow says the following word is jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: An elderly stoker has gone to bed and disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges GONE into NEGO; he is one of the three thrown into Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace in Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament youth survived the burning fiery furnace with Shadrach and Meshach.

clue.text: Day Lewis's description of Margaret as American horse?

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of Margaret
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet describes a woman called Margaret as a horse from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Day Lewis's 1957 collection is 'Pegasus and Other Poems'; the winged horse of Greek myth is the poet's steed.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged steed of Greek myth, ridden by Bellerophon, is a horse.

clue.text: Stevenson's first man on barrage

parts.note: Adam is the first man in Genesis
a barrage is a dam across a river, a weir

explanation.surface: Stevenson's original man stands on a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's unfinished Weir of Hermiston, Adam Weir is the hanging judge, Lord Hermiston.
explanation.definitionFit: The hanging judge in Stevenson's last novel is the character called by this full name.

clue.text: Moves made by Irish master to find mate

definitions.text: Moves made by Irish master to find mate

parts.words: Moves made by Irish master to find mate
parts.note: the closing moves of a chess game hunting checkmate, and the title of a play by the Irish master Samuel Beckett

explanation.surface: A chess grandmaster from Ireland plays for checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish master is Samuel Beckett, whose 1957 play takes its title from the final phase of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: The last phase of a chess game, with few pieces left, and Beckett's play about Hamm and Clov.

clue.text: It showed how sacrifices had to be made for art

definitions.text: It showed how sacrifices had to be made for art

parts.words: It showed how sacrifices had to be made for art
parts.note: reads like artistic self-denial, but describes the art of foretelling from offerings sacrificed to the gods

explanation.surface: A lesson that artists must give things up for their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrifices' and 'art' suggest an artist's self-denial; the art is divination, which read omens from sacrificial offerings.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means divination by examining sacrificial victims or offerings.

clue.text: Cleopatra to Charmian: "Pass around the vipers"

indicators.note: around says the letters of the word before it are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: The Egyptian queen asks her maid to hand round the snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges PASS; Cleopatra kills herself with the serpent's bite in Shakespeare, Charmian her attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Vipers are venomous snakes, the kind Cleopatra used.

clue.text: Ale map (showing all good pubs?) offered wrong way up by Richardson's correspondent

indicators.note: in a down clue, wrong way up means the two words are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A guide to beer houses is held upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered wrong way up' turns ALE MAP into the heroine of Samuel Richardson's epistolary novel of 1740.
explanation.definitionFit: Richardson's first novel is told through the letters its servant-girl heroine writes home.

clue.text: Northern poet supplies mystic symbol to Austrian composer

parts.note: a rune is a letter of the old Germanic alphabet with magical associations
Alban Berg, the Viennese composer

explanation.surface: A Nordic writer gives a magic sign to a Viennese musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Johan Ludvig Runeberg (1804-77) is Finland's national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Finnish national poet, who wrote in Swedish, is a writer from the far north.

clue.text: "Whatever Miss T- / Turns into Miss T" (Walter de la Mare)

definitions.text: "Whatever Miss T- / Turns into Miss T" (Walter de la Mare)

parts.words: "Whatever Miss T- / Turns into Miss T" (Walter de la Mare)
parts.note: complete the nursery verse: whatever the little lady consumes becomes part of her

explanation.surface: A line of de la Mare's children's poem with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: De la Mare's poem 'Miss T.' says that all the food she takes in turns into Miss T herself.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb is what Miss T does with her meals, consuming them as food.

clue.text: Like Capote's prayers

parts.note: Truman Capote's unfinished last novel has this word before Prayers in its title

explanation.surface: A question about how Truman Capote's prayers turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: Capote's unfinished novel is 'Answered Prayers', after St Teresa's saying that more tears are shed over prayers granted than those not.
explanation.definitionFit: Prayers that are granted have had a reply from heaven.

clue.text: Grace of Lord Calambre

parts.note: in Maria Edgeworth's The Absentee, Lord Colambre loves his cousin Grace; the clue asks her surname

explanation.surface: A question about the beloved of an Irish lord.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edgeworth's novel The Absentee (1812) Lord Colambre marries Grace; the clue spells his name Calambre.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgeworth's heroine Grace bears this surname, inherited from her family.

clue.text: It could be a sin to think inwardly in French in sort of stanza

indicators.note: inwardly puts the French verb inside the rearranged letters
it could be says the letters of the next two words are one possible rearrangement

parts.note: penser is the French verb meaning to think, as the words in French that follow say

explanation.surface: Musing inwardly in French could be sinful, in a certain verse form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be' rearranges A SIN into SIAN, and 'inwardly' sets PENSER within it, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine-line stanza of The Faerie Queene is named after its poet, Edmund Spenser.
